method: Suspect Pool thought experiment (JD's coursework document, 2026-10-27): define the pool, define a yes/no question, filter by observable behavior categories, weigh by rarity (base rates), then check the result with a prediction. Demographics are banned as categories by construction — the library below contains behavior patterns only, each tied to a real on-file snippet. Survivors are a shortlist, not a conclusion.

categories.name: Holds a leadership or logistics role
categories.definition: On file with a role that carries responsibility for people, operations, or a program.
categories.evidence_rule: A snippet naming the role (pastor, coordinator, director, president, chief, leader, organizer, founder, captain, manager, chair). Academic honors (President's List) never count.

categories.name: Has organized or run a specific activity
categories.definition: On-file text describes a specific, named activity they organized, hosted, founded, coordinated, launched, or led.
categories.evidence_rule: An action verb tied to a specific activity. Holding a title, without a described activity, does not count here.

categories.name: Shows up repeatedly, over time
categories.definition: The record shows the behavior recurring: duration language (weekly, regularly, since a year, for N years) or activity mentions spanning two or more distinct years.
categories.evidence_rule: A snippet carrying duration/repetition language, or footprint mentions of their activity in two or more distinct years.

categories.name: Volunteers, mentors, teaches, or serves on a body
categories.definition: On-file text shows them giving time to others: volunteering, mentoring, teaching, tutoring, helping, or serving on a board/council/body.
categories.evidence_rule: A service verb in the snippet. A job title containing 'Assistant' never counts.

categories.name: Hosts or gathers people
categories.definition: On-file text shows them hosting or gathering people — a home that is a gathering spot, hosting at home, a host family.
categories.evidence_rule: A snippet describing them hosting or their home gathering people. Hosting an event in the abstract does not count; that is the action category.

categories.name: Recurring correspondent on file
categories.definition: A recurring correspondent in the threads on file — someone who actually writes back, repeatedly.
categories.evidence_rule: The footprint calls them a recurring correspondent, or two or more footprint bullets cite their email threads.

pitfalls.d: Evidence that fits the category gets noticed; evidence that doesn't gets explained away.
A friend group is small. One or two data points can look like a pattern.
Once someone is labeled, later behavior gets interpreted through the label.
Background, income, or identity as categories encode assumptions rather than predict behavior — banned here by construction.
Casework profiles were tested against arrests. Social profiles usually cannot be tested, so results feel more certain than they are.
Profiling people you know, without their knowledge, can damage relationships if discovered. Private and hypothetical keeps the risk down.
